Arrays.description: A contiguous block of memory storing elements of the same type. Supports O(1) random access by index.

typical_complexities.easy: O(n) time, O(1) or O(n) space
typical_complexities.medium: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
typical_complexities.hard: O(n) or O(n log n) time, O(1) or O(n) space

Strings.description: A sequence of characters. In most languages strings are immutable, so modifications create new strings.
edge_cases: string with spaces or special characters

typical_complexities.easy: O(n) time, O(1) or O(26) space

Linked Lists.description: A linear data structure where each node holds a value and a pointer to the next node. No random access.

common_operations.delete: O(n) to find, O(1) to remove

Trees.description: A hierarchical data structure with a root node and subtrees of children. Binary trees have at most 2 children per node.

typical_complexities.easy: O(n) time, O(h) space for recursion stack

Graphs.description: A set of vertices connected by edges. Can be directed or undirected, weighted or unweighted.

common_operations.Dijkstra: O((V + E) log V) with priority queue

edge_cases: negative edge weights (use Bellman-Ford, not Dijkstra)

typical_complexities.medium: O((V+E) log V) time, O(V + E) space

Dynamic Programming.description: An optimization technique that solves problems by breaking them into overlapping subproblems and storing results to avoid recomputation.
common_patterns: 1D DP: dp[i] depends on dp[i-1] or dp[i-2]
2D DP: dp[i][j] depends on dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]
Interval DP: dp[i][j] over subarray from i to j
Bitmask DP: dp[mask] for subset problems
edge_cases: very large n requiring space optimization

typical_complexities.easy: O(n) or O(n^2) time, O(n) space
typical_complexities.medium: O(n^2) time, O(n) or O(n^2) space
typical_complexities.hard: O(n log n) or O(n^2) time, O(n) space

Sliding Window.description: A technique using a window (subarray/substring) that slides over data to efficiently compute results without restarting from scratch.
Sliding Window.when_to_use: When the problem asks for a contiguous subarray or substring satisfying some condition.

typical_complexities.medium: O(n) time, O(k) space for frequency map

Stacks and Queues.description: Stack is LIFO (Last In First Out). Queue is FIFO (First In First Out). Both support O(1) push/pop/enqueue/dequeue.
edge_cases: all elements in decreasing order (for monotonic stack)

Sorting.description: Arranging elements in a specific order. Comparison-based sorts have O(n log n) lower bound. Non-comparison sorts can be O(n).

complexities.merge_sort: O(n log n) time, O(n) space, stable
complexities.quick_sort: O(n log n) average, O(n^2) worst, O(log n) space
complexities.heap_sort: O(n log n) time, O(1) space, not stable
complexities.counting_sort: O(n + k) time, O(k) space, for small integer ranges

Binary Search.description: Efficiently finds a target in a sorted array by repeatedly halving the search space. O(log n) time.
Binary Search.template: lo=0, hi=n-1; while lo<=hi: mid=(lo+hi)//2; if arr[mid]==target: return mid; elif arr[mid]<target: lo=mid+1; else: hi=mid-1
edge_cases: target at boundaries (first or last element)
integer overflow in mid calculation (use lo + (hi-lo)//2)

typical_complexities.medium: O(log n) or O(n log n) time, O(1) space
typical_complexities.hard: O(n log n) or O(log^2 n) time, O(1) space

C++.notes: Use #include<bits/stdc++.h>, int main(), cin/cout. Vectors for arrays. Use long long for large numbers.

Python.notes: Use sys.stdin for fast input. Lists for arrays. No need for explicit types. Use collections.defaultdict, deque.

Java.notes: Use Scanner or BufferedReader. ArrayList for dynamic arrays. Use long for large numbers. Class name must be Main.

difficulty_guidelines.Easy: Single concept, straightforward implementation, O(n) or O(n log n), minimal edge cases, suitable for beginners.
difficulty_guidelines.Medium: Combines 2 concepts, requires insight or optimization, O(n log n) or O(n^2) with optimization, several edge cases.
difficulty_guidelines.Hard: Multiple concepts, non-obvious approach, tight constraints requiring optimal solution, many edge cases.
